collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A villager's necklace tells their life story: hold a festival of personal stories, or let it grow on its own.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has made a necklace with a bead for every important day of (subject.his/her) life. People keep asking about it. (friend) suggests a festival where everyone wears something that tells their story. Some villagers love the idea. Some find it too personal. What should the village do?

choices.label: Let It Grow on Its Own

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The festival is colorful and surprising: a fisher wears a hat made of every hook ever lost, a child wears a drawing of an imaginary friend. One villager wears nothing special at all, and says that is the whole story. Everyone accepts it.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: No festival is held. But after (subject)'s necklace, people start telling the stories behind their own beads, scars and tattoos at the evening fire, when they feel like it. It becomes a quiet custom.
